public_health_question.v: What work duties and PPE use did Colorado dairy farmworkers report before and after detection of A(H5N1) in cows on their farms?

ev.q: This report includes survey results describing work activities and PPE use on three dairy farms in Colorado before and after A(H5N1) outbreaks were identified.
Dairy Farmworkers Exposed to Cows Infected with Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Viruses
Personal Protective Equipment Use by Dairy Farmworkers
Colorado dairy farms with A(H5N1) virus–infected cows during July–August 2024 were eligible to participate in the retrospective survey.
PPE use, both in the weeks before and after A(H5N1) virus detection on the farm
CDPHE conducted voluntary worker surveys in English or Spanish during site visits to the three participating farms using a structured interview questionnaire.
Colorado, 2024

equity.level_reason: Interview language (87% Spanish) is reported only as a descriptor of participants; occupation is a route of exposure, not SES. No group-specific results by an SPD.

ev.q: among these, 72 (87%) were interviewed in Spanish.

equity.equity_measurement: Only interview language is reported; no race/ethnicity, nativity or SES data on workers.

notes: Convenience sample of 83 workers on three farms; all comparisons are descriptive with no CIs or tests. The before/after comparison of PPE use among exposed workers (n=44 vs 42, overlapping) is the headline; exposed vs unexposed is a secondary comparison. Public health PPE distribution is discussed as a possible reason for the increase but not formally evaluated.
view_issues: The 28% and 40% increases are not shown in tables and it is unclear whether they are relative or percentage-point changes. Text says median duties fell from five to three after detection, but Table 1 shows 5 vs 3 for unexposed vs exposed workers. Farm counts are inconsistent (64 affected farms, 43 contacted, 37 of 58 ordered PPE).
